title: Tic Tac Toe Game: Complete Design
description: Design tic tac toe game with OOP principles, class diagrams, and scalable C# implementations.

data.text: Design a tic tac toe game using object-oriented principles. Focus on clean class design, proper encapsulation, and extensible architecture.

data.caption: Class diagram for Tic Tac Toe Game. Each class encapsulates domain logic and collaborates through well-defined interfaces.

data.caption: Interaction flow for Tic Tac Toe Game. Shows how components collaborate to fulfill a user request.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as TicTacToeGameService
    participant GA as Game
    participant BO as Board
    participant PL as Player
    participant MO as Move

    C->>S: Request
    S->>BO: Start()
    BO-->>S: Result
    S->>PL: MakeMove()
    PL-->>S: Result
    S->>MO: CheckWin()
    MO-->>S: Result
    S->>MO: End()
    MO-->>S: Result
    S-->>C: Response

data.text: Extend the design with patterns like Strategy, Observer, and Factory to handle complexity and ensure the tic tac toe game scales gracefully.

data.title: tic-tac-toe-game.Advanced.cs — Processor Pipeline
Design Principles Applied
data.text: Use composition over inheritance. Keep entities simple. Use interfaces to decouple services from implementations. Apply CQRS when read and write patterns diverge.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Encapsulate state inside entities; expose behavior, not data
Strategy and Command patterns make behavior pluggable
Dependency injection keeps classes loosely coupled
data.takeaway: Tic Tac Toe Game demonstrates how clean OOP design leads to maintainable, testable code that can evolve with requirements.
